newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Financial services to be WTO meeting topic - Summers.
newsitem.headline: Financial services to be WTO meeting topic - Summers.

text.p: Liberalisation of financial services will be discussed at the World Trade Organisation (WTO) ministerial meeting in December but will not be resolved there, U.S. Treasury Deputy Secretary Lawrence Summers said on Friday.
Summers told a news conference he was sure the issue would come up in some way at the Singapore meeting of WTO member trade ministers.
"I don't expect it to be resolved...before or at the Singapore ministerial, but over time I hope we will make progress," he said.
"We regard financial services as a crucial area of the WTO negotiations," Summers said.
The United States has been at odds with a number of other nations on the pace and manner of financial services liberalisation.
Washington was "looking for commitments to move to full and effective national treatment according to some schedule" in the financial services area, Summers said.
"Over time we've certainly seen progress, but that as yet we've not seen enough progress to permit us to make the final irrevocable commitment," Summers said.
